# Repository Guidance — tabletop-dice-roller-support

## Work authority

Open GitHub Issues are the sole authoritative backlog for planned/actionable work unless this repo's flavor explicitly defines a different authority model.

README files, design notes, roadmaps, comments, and Git history are context. Do not mine prose as a hidden task queue or treat speculative documentation as implementation authorization.

Before changing anything, read the relevant Issue/request plus surrounding implementation and applicable docs. Do not infer architecture from filenames alone.

## Ambiguity and assumptions

- Resolve uncertainty from repository state before asking the user or guessing: inspect the relevant Issue/request, source, tests, configuration, authoritative docs, and recent history as appropriate.
- If sources conflict, identify the conflict and prefer the explicit current request plus the repository's designated authority model over stale or speculative prose.
- Ask only when a material decision cannot be resolved safely from available repository evidence.
- Never invent missing facts, validation results, environment details, or user intent.

## Cross-project provenance

- Whenever an agent intentionally crosses a project or repository boundary for work that influences the current task, leave a durable trace in the originating project's current Issue, PR, or other authoritative work record before ending the session.
- Record the other project/repository, what was read/called/changed, why the boundary was crossed, and the concrete result or reference (Issue, PR, branch, commit, workflow/deployment run, release, artifact, or equivalent).
- Read-only cross-project calls may be summarized briefly, but they still require enough provenance to reconstruct which external project informed the work.
- If the cross-project action mutates, deploys, publishes, releases, or configures the target project, leave a reciprocal trace in the target project's relevant durable record when possible so the relationship can be reconstructed from either side.
- For deployment or publishing flows, explicitly record which repository/project owns the production deployment and how the cross-project handoff was invoked.
- Never rely on chat/session history as the only documentation of a cross-project interaction.

## Validation truthfulness

- Run the smallest relevant validation plus broader checks required by scope.
- Never claim a test, browser/device check, deployment, server run, account action, or external-system validation unless it actually occurred.
- Distinguish static/local validation from real integration/environment validation.
- State exactly what remains unverified.

## Working style

This is a solo/hobby-oriented repo ecosystem. Avoid process for process's sake.

- Prefer focused changes over broad rewrites.
- Preserve working architecture unless redesign is requested.
- Significant behavioral, architectural, dependency, release/build, security, or cross-system changes should use a focused branch/PR.
- Keep PRs purpose-specific.
- Keep actionable work in the designated authority system rather than creating alternate backlog files.
- Track unrelated newly discovered work separately unless fixing it is necessary to complete the current task safely.

## Support-repository authority model

This repository is public support/triage, not product source.

- Use Issues to receive, clarify, and triage reports/requests.
- Do not implement product changes here.
- Route engineering work to the designated source repository.
- Preserve reproduction evidence, version/context, and reporter privacy.
- Never ask reporters to expose secrets or sensitive private data.
